newsitem.title: GERMANY: German call rates start week little changed.
newsitem.headline: German call rates start week little changed.

text.p: German call rates were steady around 3.07 percent to 3.10 percent on Monday with traders saying liquidy was well positioned to meet expected reserve requirements.

Traders said that with money conditions fairly even, they expected the Bundesbank to neither provide a net drain, nor a net addition to the market on Wednesday when a 71.9 billion mark repo pact expires.
"The balances look good," one trader said. "From the preliminary figures, I would expect an unchanged tender allocation."
Credit institutions held 41.4 billion marks with the Bundesbank on Friday, leaving the average for the month as of Sunday at 40.5 billion marks.
No appreciable amount of funds was borrowed from the emergency Lombard lending facility.
The Frankfurt Interbank Overnight Average FIONA= stood at 3.13567 percent on Monday compared with 3.11633 percent on Friday.
